source_text:
Testamentum ad cives
∆ιαθήκη πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας.
31 προτείνουσι δ' οὖν ὅμως διαθήκην πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας διατεταγμένην, καθ'
ἣν μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας ἢ ἐν κοιμητηρίοις παρεγγυᾷ. 32 προσέχετε
ἑαυτοῖς καὶ κρατεῖτε τὰς παραδόσεις ἃς παρελάβετε· μὴ ἐκκλίνητε δεξιὰ μηδὲ
ἀριστερά. 33 καὶ ἐν τούτῳ μνήμην ἔχετε, τέκνα ἀγαπητά, τοῦ μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας
ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας μήτε ἐν τοῖς κοιμητηρίοις τῶν ἁγίων· ἀλλ' ἀεὶ διὰ μνήμης ἔχετε τὸν
θεὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν. ἀλλ' οὔτε κατ' οἶκον κοινόν· οὐκ ἔξεστι γὰρ Χριστιανῷ
δι' ὀφθαλμῶν μετεωρίζεσθαι καὶ ῥεμβασμῶν τοῦ νοός, ἀλλ' ἐγγεγραμμένα καὶ
ἐντετυπωμένα ἔστω πᾶσι τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν. 34 εἴ τις τὸν θεῖον τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου
χαρακτῆρα κατὰ τὴν σάρκωσιν ἐξ ὑλικῶν χρωμάτων ἐπιτηδεύει κατανοῆσαι... ἔστω
ἀνάθεμα.
thought_title: Prohibition of images in churches, cemeteries, and homes
orientation: Epiphanius is issuing a binding testament to the citizens, commanding them not to bring images into churches or the cemeteries of the saints.
pass_a_gloss: They put forward, then, nevertheless, a testament to the citizens, an ordered testament, according to which he urges not to bring up images onto churches or in cemeteries. Pay attention to yourselves and hold fast the traditions which you received; do not turn aside to the right nor to the left. And in this matter keep memory, beloved children, of not bringing up images onto churches nor in the cemeteries of the saints; but always through memory keep God in your hearts. But not even in an ordinary house; for it is not lawful for a Christian to be distracted through the eyes and wanderings of the mind, but let the things toward God be written and impressed in all. If anyone deliberately endeavors to depict the divine character of God's word according to the incarnation from material colors... let him be anathema.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'testament' for this binding ordinance; banned alternatives include covenant, decree, ordinance.
Glossary requires 'images' for religious pictures; banned alternatives include effigies, icons, idols.
Glossary requires 'cemeteries' for burial places of the saints; banned alternatives include dormitories, resting places, sleeping places.
Glossary requires 'traditions' for things handed down; banned alternatives include customs, ordinances, teachings handed down.
Glossary requires 'anathema' for the solemn condemnation; banned alternatives include accursed, condemned, excommunicated.
Glossary requires 'character' for the divine imprint of God's Word in the incarnation; banned alternatives include exact representation, imprint, stamp.

pass_b_english: He presents a testament to the citizens, a binding testament, in which he urges them not to bring images into churches or into the cemeteries. "Pay attention to yourselves and hold fast the traditions you received. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left. And in this matter, beloved children, keep memory: do not bring images into churches or into the cemeteries of the saints. Instead, always keep God in memory in your hearts. But not even in an ordinary house is this permitted, for a Christian must not be distracted through the eyes and the wanderings of the mind. Let the things toward God be written and impressed on all. If anyone deliberately endeavors to depict the divine character of God's Word according to the incarnation from material colors, let him be anathema."

last_rejected.quote: They present a testament to the citizens, a binding testament, in which he urges them
last_rejected.source_quote: προτείνουσι δ' οὖν ὅμως διαθήκην πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας διατεταγμένην, καθ' ἣν μὴ ἀναφέρειν εἰκόνας ἐπ' ἐκκλησίας ἢ ἐν κοιμητηρίοις παρεγγυᾷ
last_rejected.why: Subject shifts from plural 'they' to singular 'he' with no antecedent; source has no explicit subject, but context suggests Epiphanius's community or successors present it, while 'he' (Epiphanius) commands.
last_rejected.fix: A binding testament is presented to the citizens, in which he urges them
last_rejected.ruling: Greek has no explicit subjects; 'they'/'he' reflects implied agents. Standard for subjectless Greek verbs. Not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Third-person plural 'they' hides that no first-person authorial voice exists per brief; 'they' introduces unnamed agents, confusing voice attribution.
last_rejected.fix: A binding testament is presented to the citizens
last_rejected.ruling: προτείνουσι is 3rd plural; 'they' is grammatically warranted. No first-person voice exists in source clause.

last_rejected.why: Ellipsis in source (εἴ τις...ἐπιτηδεύει κατανοῆσαι...ἔστω ἀνάθεμα) implies 'let him be anathema' but English omits the conditional's full force; more critically, 'beloved children' (τέκνα ἀγαπητά) vocative is present but 'saints' (τῶν ἁγίων) is rendered, checking: actually 'beloved children' is present. Re-checking: no, 'beloved children' is in English. The ellipsis '...' in source after κατανοῆσαι is preserved in sense. However: 'ἀλλ' οὔτε κατ' οἶκον κοινόν' — 'not even in a common house' — English has 'But not even in a common house is this permitted' which adds 'is this permitted' not in source. That's addition, not omission. Re-checking for actual omission: 'ἐγγεγραμμένα καὶ ἐντετυπωμένα ἔστω πᾶσι τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν' — 'Let what pertains to God be written and impressed on all.' Source says 'on all' (πᾶσι, dative), English has 'on all' — correct. No clear omission found; retracting.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker retracted; no omission confirmed. English renders all key elements including τέκνα ἀγαπητά and ἔστω ἀνάθεμα.
